column3: Close to the Hebrew; “the oracle” is rendered “The burden.”
Close to the Hebrew; “mischief” is rendered “trouble,” and “devastation” “plundering.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the law grows numb” is rendered “the law is powerless,” and “justice perverted” “perverse judgment.”
Close to the Hebrew; “impetuous” is rendered “hasty.”
Close to the Hebrew; “keen” is rendered “more fierce,” and “its warhorses paw the ground” “Their chargers charge ahead.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the totality of their faces [is] eastward” is rendered “Their faces are set like the east wind”; the meaning of the word is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “it heaped up earth” is rendered “they heap up earthen mounds.”

NKJV renders “then it swept on [like] a wind and passed on, and is guilty, whose strength is his god” as “Then his mind changes, and he transgresses; He commits offense, Ascribing this power to his god.”
Close to the Hebrew; “you have appointed it … established it” is rendered “You have appointed them … marked them.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV continues the question from verse 13 (“Why do You make men”).
Close to the Hebrew; the singular “he” is rendered as plural, “They.”
Close to the Hebrew; the singular is rendered as plural, and “his portion is fat” “their share is sumptuous.”
Close to the Hebrew; the singular is rendered as plural (“Shall they … empty their net”).
